newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thai state oil firm to invest $240 mln in Manila.
newsitem.headline: Thai state oil firm to invest $240 mln in Manila.

text.p: State-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) said on Friday it will invest $240 million over the next five years to put up 140 petroleum service stations in the Philippines.
PTT said the first petroleum service station will be opened in November in Subic in the northern Philippines.
PTT has formed a wholly-owned subsidiary PTT Philippines Inc to establish its oil retail business in the country, Viset Choopiban, PTT executive director said in a statement.
The Thai firm said it will also set up four joint venture companies with Coastal Corp, a unit of Coastal Petroleum, to conduct petroleum business in the Philippines.

But PTT did not elaborate on the activities of its proposed four joint venture firms. The companies are Subic Bay Petroleum Products (Cayman Islands) Ltd., Subic Bay Petroleum Products (Philippines) Inc, Pipeline and Clark Development Company and Subic Bay Distribution Inc.
PTT will be the first foreign oil company to put up petroleum service stations in the Philippines after the government started partial deregulation of the oil industry last June.
